sections.label: Holistic debate on both Bills
sections.summary: This allows a holistic debate so Members can raise questions on both Bills, while the formal Second Reading of the Shared Mobility Enterprises (Control and Licensing) Bill still deals with procedural requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This will allow a holistic debate and enable Members to raise questions or express their views on both Bills during the debate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We will still have the formal Second Reading of the Shared Mobility Enterprises (Control and Licensing) Bill to ensure that procedural requirements are dealt with.

sections.label: Extending footpath ban to motorised PMDs
sections.summary: After the November 2019 e-scooter footpath ban, footpath accidents involving PMDs fell 52%, and the Active Mobility (Amendment) Bill 2020 extends the footpath ban to all motorised PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In November 2019, we reviewed our regulations and took the difficult but necessary step to ban e-scooters from footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Since then, footpath accidents involving PMDs have reduced by 52% and sentiments towards public path safety have improved.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The Active Mobility (Amendment) Bill 2020 gives effect to our earlier announced intention to extend the ban on footpaths to all motorised PMDs.

sections.label: Theory test for certain riders
sections.summary: Riders of certain active mobility devices, called test-needed-to-drive vehicles in the Bill, must pass a theory test before they are allowed to ride.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To improve awareness of the rules, regulations and expected safe-riding behaviours, we will require riders of certain active mobility devices – which we call “test-needed-to-drive vehicles” in the Bill – to pass a theory test before they are allowed to ride.

sections.label: Mandatory inspection regime for e-scooters
sections.summary: New sections 35A, 35B and 35C introduce a mandatory inspection regime starting with e-scooters, which must be inspected and certified compliant with prescribed criteria such as weight, width, speed and UL2272 certification.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Through the new sections 35A, 35B and 35C of the Bill, we will introduce a mandatory inspection regime, starting with e-scooters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Riders will only be able to ride on public paths, e-scooters that have been inspected and certified to be compliant with the prescribed device criteria, such as those relating to weight, width, speed and UL2272 certification.

sections.label: Doubled speeding penalties
sections.summary: The penalty for a first-time offender speeding on public paths is doubled from $1,000 and/or three months' imprisonment to $2,000 and/or six months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For example, the penalty for a first-time offender caught speeding on public paths will be doubled from $1,000 and/or three months' imprisonment to $2,000 and/or six months' imprisonment.

sections.label: Higher penalty for selling non-compliant devices
sections.summary: The penalty for selling a non-compliant device for use on public paths rises more than four times, from $5,000 and/or three months' imprisonment to $20,000 and/or 24 months' imprisonment for a first-time individual offender.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For example, the penalty for selling a non-compliant device for use on public paths will be increased by more than four times, from $5,000 and/or three months' imprisonment to $20,000 and/or 24 months' imprisonment, for a first-time offender who is an individual.

sections.label: Shared Mobility Enterprises Bill licensing expansion
sections.summary: The Bill expands licensing to cover public safety, all active mobility device-sharing services, and a class licence regime.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The Shared Mobility Enterprises Bill will expand the current licensing regime in the PPA in three main ways.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: First, we will extend the scope of the regulatory regime beyond controlling indiscriminate parking to also focus on public safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Second, we will expand our licensing coverage to all active mobility device-sharing services, for devices that can be used on public paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Third, we will have the powers to introduce a class licence regime to allow us to apply a differentiated and light-touch regime on operators whose business model or operations may pose less safety or parking concerns.

sections.label: Miscellaneous amendments and regulatory approach
sections.summary: The Bill extends the false information offence to all LTA applications under AMA and adjusts regulation for public path safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Apart from tightening regulations on active mobility device users, retailers, businesses and device-sharing operators, the Bill makes several miscellaneous amendments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: These include extending the offence of giving false information to cover all applications that persons make to LTA under AMA, beyond just applications to register a PMD.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We must continue to adjust our regulatory approach to keep pace with technological and market developments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: These two Bills together make sure that we have an approach that covers the device riders, retailers, businesses and device-sharing operators, with the principle of establishing public path safety as the primary intention, and provides us the tools and measures to intervene further should they become necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This set of Bills will ensure safer paths for Singaporeans while promoting active mobility.

sections.label: Riders trained since November
sections.summary: Since November last year until now, 63 riders have undergone training for various modules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Since November last year until now, 63 riders have undergone training for various modules.

sections.label: Licensing food delivery operators
sections.summary: The passage asks whether operators must be required before operating and whether LTA would license food delivery operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will we be, therefore, requiring the operator to do so before allowing them to operate such a platform here in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, would LTA be looking at licensing the food delivery operators, similar to what was done for the third-party ride-hailing apps?

sections.label: Considering licensing operators long term
sections.summary: The passage says in the longer term it may need to consider licensing operators so responsible actions become industry standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While we are happy to see those businesses continue to protect and look into the riders' interest but, in the longer term, we may need to consider whether we need to license the operators so that the responsible actions of a few will be the standard for all that are in the industry.

sections.label: E-scooter and e-bike rider requirements
sections.summary: E-scooter and e-bike users must be at least 16 years old and take a theory test to ride on public paths.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: E-scooter and e-bike users must be at least 16 years old and take a theory test to ride on public paths.

sections.label: PMA access and rider insurance
sections.summary: The speaker suggests easing PMA access for those with light mobility problems and notes third-party liability insurance now covers e-scooter riders and other mobility device users at work.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If so, we might have to make it easier for those with light mobility problems to get PMAs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that my persistent push for third-party liability insurance for e-scooter riders has finally paid off.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Businesses are now required to cover their riders who use e-scooters for work with third-party liability insurance, and this requirement is also extended to those who use other mobility devices for work.

sections.label: E-scooter trade-in grant applications
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min revealed 3,550 riders applied for the e-scooter trade-in grant, about three-quarters choosing PABs and a quarter bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min revealed that 3,550 riders have applied for the e-scooter trade-in grant, with about three-quarters of those opting for PABs and a quarter going for bicycles.

sections.label: PMD footpath ban and measures
sections.summary: The speaker says residents no longer felt scared after the PMD footpath ban and welcomes measures including minimum age 16, training and third-party insurance.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Many residents have told me that ever since the ban of PMDs on footpaths, they no longer felt scared every day.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that measures that I have been repeatedly calling for are finally being implemented, including the minimum age requirement of 16 for PMD users, training and third-party insurance.

sections.label: Riders switching to PABs and bicycles
sections.summary: Over 3,000 delivery riders switched from PMDs to PABs or bicycles, and e-scooters will be allowed on cycling paths, with the network extended to 750 km by 2025 and 1,300 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government has also revealed that there were more than 3,000 delivery riders who have switched from PMDs to PABs or bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What impact will it have when there are more PABs and bicycles on the road?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We must ensure that these riders have proper training, we legislate against drink-cycling and make sure that PABs comply with the fire regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: He had also announced that e-scooters will be allowed on cycling paths and the Ministry of Transport (MOT) will step up the construction of such cycling paths to provide clear separation between pedestrians and e-scooters, extending the network of cycling paths from 440 kilometres (km) to 750 km latest by 2025 and to 1,300 km by 2030.

sections.label: LTA enforcement officer numbers
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min said on 4 November 2019 that LTA had 174 enforcement officers, a number the speaker found surprisingly unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min mentioned on 4 November 2019 that LTA had 174 enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I was a little surprised that, by that time, the number of officers had remained only at that level.

sections.label: Public education and safe riding certification
sections.summary: The speaker says sufficient public education will help develop the right riding culture and asks the Government to reconsider mandatory safe riding certification courses with disqualification rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Having sufficient public education to inform and ensure all PMD users as well as pedestrians know what is allowed and not allowed will go a long way to ensure that the right riding culture is developed ultimately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Government to also reconsider one of the questions I have asked in my Parliamentary Question on 4 November 2019, namely, that the Government should consider mandatory safe riding certification courses with disqualification rights.

sections.label: Mandatory competency test for e-scooter users
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a mandatory competency test, and the speaker hopes shared e-scooter services will be limited to users who pass it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In that connection, I am happy that a mandatory competency test will be introduced by this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the context of this Active Mobility (Amendment) Bill and the Shared Mobility Enterprises (Control and Licensing) Bill introducing new regulations for shared mobility services, I hope that shared e-scooter services will only be available to users who have passed a mandatory or competency test.

sections.label: Regulating after-market batteries
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOT would regulate after-market batteries sold separately, including testing and supply, and work with Singapore Customs to bar imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would MOT consider specifically regulating after-market batteries, sold separately from the devices, including testing and supply, so that access to batteries which do not conform to requisite safety standards is denied completely, thereby avoiding fire risks from their use?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In addition to inspections, MOT can work with Singapore Customs to bar import of off-specs batteries, including via individual online purchases.

sections.label: Expansion of cycling paths
sections.summary: Plans have been announced to expand Singapore's 440 km of cycling paths to 750 km by 2025 and about 1,300 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Factoring walking into the equation is especially critical as plans have been announced to expand the 440 km of cycling paths here to 750 km by 2025 and about 1,300 km by 2030.

sections.label: NUS research on walkability issues
sections.summary: NUS research identified issues with poor walkability of Singapore's housing estates along connectivity, closeness and spatial distribution, comfort and safety.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Research by Zhang, Azzali, Janssen and Stouffs at School of Design and Environment at the National University of Singapore (NUS) identified several issues pertaining to poor walkability of Singapore's housing estates along four different dimensions: connectivity, closeness and spatial distribution, comfort and safety.

sections.label: Factors in qualitative walkability research
sections.summary: Using qualitative research methods, the researchers identified convenience, health, comfort and time-cost savings as the most critical factors.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Using qualitative research methods, they identified convenience, health, comfort and time-cost savings as being the most critical factors.

sections.label: Walkability and third-party insurance requirement
sections.summary: Improving walkability in HDB estates must be key, and under new section 58A businesses must ensure drivers and riders have third-party insurance.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Improving walkability in HDB estates must, therefore, be a key tranche of our overall plans for active mobility and should not be an afterthought.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the new section 58A, businesses will be required to ensure that the drivers and riders they engage or employ are covered by third-party insurance, whether the vehicles utilised are regular or PABs, PMDs, motorised wheelchairs or mobility scooters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In the event of an accident, the insurance coverage will ensure that the victims will be able to claim medical expenses as well as compensation for any other damages.

sections.label: Victims without insurance seek recourse
sections.summary: Without insurance, victims can only attempt private settlements through mediation or civil claims, and some residents sought help from the speaker.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Without insurance, victims can only try for private settlements through mediation or make civil claims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I have had a few cases where my residents who were victims approached me for help as they were unable to seek any recourse.

sections.label: Bicycles in bike-sharing schemes
sections.summary: In September 2018, 100,000 bicycles from different bike-sharing schemes were in circulation, alongside public outcry over irresponsible rider behaviours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In September 2018, a total of 100,000 bicycles were in circulation across the island from different bike-sharing schemes that also saw a public outcry of irresponsible rider behaviours.

sections.label: E-scooter and PMD regulations timeline
sections.summary: Registration of e-scooters began in February 2018, followed by measures in August and September 2019, ending in a footpath ban on 4 November 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Registration of e-scooters was the first patch fix in February 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Then, came another in August 2019 to limit speed and mandate helmets, and another in September to mandate theory tests, disallow handphones and third-party liability insurance before culminating in the overnight ban of PMDs from footpaths on 4 November 2019.

sections.label: E-scooter grant and delivery rider hardship
sections.summary: A S$7 million e-scooter Trade-in Grant came on 8 November after delivery riders met MPs, and Seline skipped meals after her husband's work dropped.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A corrective action was finally taken on 8 November through the S$7 million e-scooter Trade-in Grant scheme only after delivery riders gathered across Singapore to speak to their Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Immediately following the ban on 4 November, Seline, a resident in a rental flat, often skipped her meals with only water so that her four children can go to bed with their stomachs full, because her husband, Sengchiy, who was with three different food delivery companies went from working every day to three days' worth of work after being told off by enforcement officers to get off footpaths.

sections.label: Clause 23 sharing information refusal
sections.summary: In the Shared Mobility Enterprises Bill, clause 23 lets licensees share information to refuse hire to individuals who park improperly three times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the Shared Mobility Enterprises Bill, clause 23 allows for licensees to share information to refuse hire to particular individuals if they park improperly after three times.

sections.label: Clause 23 rationale and minimum riding age
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State to clarify clause 23's rationale and protections, and asks if the minimum riding age will be 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State please clarify the rationale for such a provision in clause 23 and what protection is given to the individuals?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Then, there is section 23A of the Active Mobility (Amendment) Bill that makes it punishable for an underage rider with fine and/or imprisonment riding a motorised PMD on shared paths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the Bill does not explicitly define what constitutes as "prescribed minimum riding age" as that will be subject to prescribed regulations where there may be different minimum riding ages for different classes or descriptions of PMDs, I would like to ask the Minister if he still intends to prescribe the minimum riding age as 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This was announced by the Ministry on 4 December 2019 in the press release accepting all recommendations from AMAP.

sections.label: Enforcement officer powers and warnings
sections.summary: Sections 47 and 50 of the Active Mobility (Amendment) Bill give AMEOs power to order riders to produce competency test certificates, seize them and deliver vehicles for inspection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last but not least, sections 47 and 50 of the Active Mobility (Amendment) Bill will give Active Mobility Enforcement Officers (AMEOs) the power to order the rider to produce his competency test certificate for examination and then seize the certificate and deliver the vehicle for an inspection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We know that as many as 6,000 warnings were issued in December 2019 and, in the same month, an Auxiliary Police Officer (APO) sent an e-scooter rider flying at Bedok Reservoir Road.

sections.label: Compulsory third-party liability insurance
sections.summary: The Bill makes third-party liability insurance compulsory for businesses, while the speaker called for it to be compulsory for all users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, there is one area that the AMAP's proposal and mine differs and that has to do with insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill seeks to make it compulsory for third-party liability insurance (TPLI) for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I have, however, called for TPLI to be made compulsory for all users.

sections.label: Summonses and impounded PMDs
sections.summary: The passage asks how many summonses have been issued since the ban took effect on 1 January and how many PMDs have been impounded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: First, how many summonses have been issued since the ban took effect on 1 January and how many PMDs have since been impounded?

sections.label: Ban on non-UL2272 batteries
sections.summary: The passage states a date of Sunday, 2 February at 10.30 pm, after the ban on non-UL2272 batteries took effect on 1 January 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This was dated Sunday, 2 February at 10.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And this is after our ban on non-UL2272 batteries that took effect on 1 January 2020.

sections.label: Tightened active mobility regulations
sections.summary: The Bill and policy efforts have progressively tightened regulations on active mobility devices covering design, construction, speed limits, user behaviour and a ban on footpath use.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Likewise, this Bill and our policy efforts have progressively tightened regulations on active mobility devices to consider design and construction, speed limits, user behaviour and, now, a ban on footpath use.

sections.label: Third-party liability insurance requirement
sections.summary: New section 58A of the Active Mobility Act requires shared mobility enterprises, employers and work platforms to ensure third-party liability insurance for their active mobility device users.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is the principle adopted for motor vehicles for decades.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill partially addresses the problem of liability with the new section 58A of the Active Mobility Act.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We will now require shared mobility enterprises, employers and work platforms, such as delivery companies, to ensure that third-party liability insurance is provided for their active mobility device users.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Basic insurance could be required at the time of purchase or registration of the active mobility device.

sections.label: PMD versus bicycle accidents
sections.summary: PMD accidents are more likely to be severe, but 2018 PMD accidents totalled one-sixth of bicycle accidents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The data shows that PMD accidents are more likely to be severe.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the total number of PMD accidents in 2018 was only one-sixth that of bicycle accidents.

sections.label: Footpath ban and delivery riders
sections.summary: The footpath ban affected 7,000 food delivery riders who relied on PMDs, and a $7 million trade-in grant helps them transition.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To what extent do active mobility devices actually help improve Singaporeans' ability to earn a living?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We knew that the footpath ban would affect 7,000 food delivery riders who relied on PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The scale of our misunderstanding was laid bare when hundreds of delivery riders turned up at hon Members’ Meet-the-People-Sessions to petition against the policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I commend the Government for addressing their concerns with the $7 million trade-in grant to help them transition to other types of transport.

sections.label: Shared bike industry collapse
sections.summary: Regulations constrained reckless shared bike supply, the industry collapsed, and licensing now minimises risks from unsustainable business models.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the Parking Places (Amendment) Act 2018 and other regulations have since then helped to constrain the reckless oversupply of shared bikes, the industry has also collapsed because the economics simply did not work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The former operators have, in some cases, left huge unrecoverable debts to stakeholders, and there are also the costs of cleaning up defunct bikes, which have been borne by LTA, the Town Councils and private landowners.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the start of licensing for shared mobility enterprises, we now have the regulatory levers to ensure that risks from unsustainable business models on society and stakeholders are minimised.

sections.label: Subsidising shared mobility enterprises
sections.summary: Shared mobility enterprises should be subsidised on the same basis as public transport only if they prove a meaningful contribution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Instead, if we believe that a shared mobility enterprise can contribute to our public transport system, we must be prepared to prove that it makes a meaningful contribution and subsidise it on the same basis as the rest of our public transport.

sections.label: Gig workers in 2018
sections.summary: MOM's 2018 Labour Force survey found around 210,000 gig workers, of whom 160,000 did this as their primary job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to MOM’s Labour Force survey of 2018, there are around 210,000 gig workers or what the Ministry calls own account workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Of these, eight in 10, or 160,000 of them, did this as their primary job.

sections.label: Driver and deliverymen numbers
sections.summary: Managing reactions could reduce policy options, and there are 41,000 PDVL drivers, 7,000 PMD deliverymen and more non-PMD deliverymen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The need to manage such reactions would reduce our policy options and it might even dissuade us from doing the right thing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There are 41,000 Private Hire Car Driver's Vocational Licence (PDVL) drivers, 7,000 PMD deliverymen and many more non-PMD deliverymen.

sections.label: Classifying gig workers as employees
sections.summary: The speaker says the step is in the right direction but not enough, and proposes classifying gig workers as employees under the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is definitely a step in the right direction but it is almost certainly not enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I propose we go a few steps further and classify gig workers as employees instead of contractors under the Employment Act.

sections.label: Gig worker opt-in and PMD rules
sections.summary: The speaker suggests gig workers could opt in and out of the Employment Act, and lists bans, tests and licensing for PMDs and bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Another option is for gig workers to have the choice to opt in and out of the Employment Act depending on their specific situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I believe that this would be a pro-people, pro-worker and pro-business message to help create the policy space we need to continue to pursue the right policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In response to dangerous riding, we are banning PMDs from footpaths, introducing competency tests and mandating adult supervision of underage users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In response to careless parking, we are requiring bicycle, PMD and PMA providers to obtain a licence and follow standards.

sections.label: Clarifying section 23 information sharing
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify what information may be shared under section 23 and how privacy compliance, penalties and class licensees are handled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is possible that some organisations will seek to acquire private users' information under the pretence of identifying bad parkers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It would be helpful if the Minister could clarify: (a) what types of information are allowed to be shared under section 23; (b) how would the Ministry ascertain whether an information transfer complies with privacy standards; (c) what regulation and penalties will prevent organisations from using section 23 as a possible loophole for PDPA; (d) finally, will section 23 apply to class licensees?

sections.label: Imprisonment for underage PMD riding
sections.summary: The new section 23A(2) provides imprisonment as a punishment option for underage riding of a motorised PMD on a shared path.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 23A(2) provides imprisonment as a punishment option for underage riding of a motorised PMD on a shared path.

sections.label: Proactive active mobility and cycling network
sections.summary: The speaker says active mobility policy should be more proactive and less reactive, and welcomes plans to triple the cycling network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But our policy towards active mobility should be more proactive and less reactive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened by the recent announcement that we will be accelerating our plans to triple the length of our cycling network.

sections.label: Cyclists and SecureMyBike parking
sections.summary: The speaker says cyclists do not need over-engineered, far-flung parking spaces like SecureMyBike, which recently closed down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What cyclists need are not over-engineered, far-flung parking spaces like SecureMyBike, the automated underground system that recently closed down.

sections.label: Cycling networks and bicycle freeways
sections.summary: Cycling networks are a patchwork of local connectivity, and ambitious infrastructure such as bicycle freeways is needed for cycling to become a true mode of transportation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even with LTA's new expansion plans, our cycling networks are currently a patchwork of local connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But if we want cycling to become a true mode of transportation, we have to build ambitious infrastructure, such as bicycle freeways, like the North-South Corridor.

sections.label: PMD numbers and accidents
sections.summary: By end-2019 there were about 100,000 PMDs in Singapore, with almost 300 PMD-related accidents in 2018 and 2019 estimated similar or higher.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: By the end of 2019, it was estimated that there were about 100,000 PMDs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As shared by MOT in a Parliament Sitting in November 2019, there were almost 300 PMD-related accidents in 2018 and the number of accidents for 2019 is estimated to be in the similar range, if not higher.

sections.label: PMD footpath ban expanded
sections.summary: The AMA amendments expand the PMD footpath ban to all device forms, including hoverboards and electric unicycles, except motorised wheelchairs, which remain allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendments to AMA stipulate that the ban of PMDs on footpaths will be expanded to cover all forms of devices, including hoverboards and electric unicycles, except for motorised wheelchairs which are still allowed on footpaths.

sections.label: Curtailing deviant riding enforcement
sections.summary: It asks how the Government proposes to curtail deviant riding and whether it can share the number of riders taken to task since the November 2019 footpath ban.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How would the Government propose to curtail such deviant riding and can the Government share any information perhaps on the number of riders that have been taken to task since the footpath ban came into effect in November 2019?

sections.label: Amendments and socially-responsible riding
sections.summary: The amendments address some immediate problems but will not guarantee no more accidents from errant PMD riding, so riders should ride in a socially-responsible manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While these amendments will help address some immediate problems, they will not guarantee that there are no more accidents as a result of errant PMD riding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I thus hope that our PMD riders and users will also play their part by riding in a socially-responsible manner as we progress towards our goal of a car-lite community that is safe for everyone – both PMD users and pedestrians.

sections.label: Third-party liability insurance for riders
sections.summary: Companies must ensure their riders use compliant devices, and companies employing or contracting active mobility device riders must ensure riders have third-party liability insurance for bodily injury and death.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Companies should also ensure their riders use devices that comply with our active mobility regulations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We will require all companies who employ or contract with active mobility device riders to ensure that their riders are covered by third-party liability insurance for bodily injury and death.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This will protect victims in the event of accidents.

sections.label: Shared Mobility Bill information sharing
sections.summary: Section 23 of the Shared Mobility Enterprises Bill enables information sharing between licensed device-sharing operators to impose a collective ban on individuals who persistently park devices improperly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Ms Anthea Ong, Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and Mr Louis Ng have asked about information sharing and specifically, the issues around section 23 of the Shared Mobility Enterprises Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This enables information sharing between the licensed device-sharing operators to effectively impose a collective ban on individuals who persistently park active mobility devices improperly.

sections.label: LTA power over user deposits
sections.summary: The Shared Mobility Enterprises Bill proposes to give LTA the power to prohibit licensees from collecting user deposits if the need arises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The Shared Mobility Enterprises Bill, therefore, proposes to give LTA the power to prohibit licensees from collecting user deposits, if the need arises.

sections.label: PAB rider age and licensing
sections.summary: PAB riders must be 16 or above, and going forward will need to pass a theory test and be licensed by TP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: PAB riders already have to be 16 years of age or above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But going forward, PAB riders will need to pass a theory test covering on-road regulations and the Highway Code and be licensed by TP.

sections.label: Non-UL2272 PMD sale and use
sections.summary: The sale of non-UL2272 PMDs was stopped in July 2019, and their use will be stopped in July 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The sale of non-UL2272 PMDs was actually stopped in July 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And the use of non-UL2272 devices will be stopped in July 2020.

sections.label: AMAP staged insurance approach
sections.summary: AMAP consulted widely and recommended a staged approach, starting with imposing insurance on businesses before extending it to individuals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: AMAP had consulted widely on this issue and they have recommended that the Government take a staged approach, starting first with imposing insurance on businesses before extending it to individuals.

sections.label: Non-compliant PMDs banned from paths
sections.summary: From 1 July 2020, non-UL2272-certified devices will not be allowed to be used on all paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Mr Alex Yam has asked about non-compliant PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I reiterate that from 1 July 2020, these non-UL2272-certified devices will not be allowed to be used on all paths.

sections.label: Mandatory e-scooter inspection regime
sections.summary: After 1 April 2020, a mandatory inspection regime for e-scooters will verify compliance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: After 1 April 2020, there will also be a mandatory inspection regime for e-scooters to verify compliance.

sections.label: Age limit for e-scooters
sections.summary: At this point in time, it is 16 years and only applies to e-scooters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: At this point in time, it is 16 years and only apply to e-scooters.

sections.label: Supervisor liability for underage riders
sections.summary: Supervisors are not liable for an underage rider's offence, but can be responsible for improper supervision without reasonable measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If an underage rider commits an offence, it will not fall on the supervisor to be liable for that offence, for example, speeding or reckless riding.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But the supervisor can be held responsible for improper supervision if he or she did not take reasonable and practical measures to ensure that the underage rider would not commit such offences.

sections.label: Banning e-scooters from footpaths
sections.summary: A fundamental review led to the difficult decision to ban e-scooters from footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Hence, we had to fundamentally review how we envisioned active mobility devices co-existing safely with other road and path users.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we made the difficult decision to ban e-scooters from footpaths.

sections.label: E-scooter Trade-in Grant applications
sections.summary: Over 3,700 e-scooter Trade-in Grant applications were approved, with about one-third of riders switched and the rest expected soon.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We received feedback that many of them have found the package of measures reassuring and useful.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have approved to date more than 3,700 applications for the e-scooter Trade-in Grant and about one-third of the riders have already successfully switched to an alternative device, with the rest expected to do so in the next couple of months.

sections.label: Safe riding conduct rules
sections.summary: One should not ride against traffic and must remain in control and progress safely and orderly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: One should not ride against traffic and one must remain in control of one's vehicle and ride, drive or progress in a safe and orderly manner.

sections.label: Minimum age for riders
sections.summary: The Member clarifies support for a minimum rider age, with officers given operational leeway to deal with circumstances differently.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, I just want to clarify that the Member does support that there is a minimum age for the riders and, hence, someone who is below that age has committed an offence or transgression at the very least.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, I think how the officers deal with that, we need to give them the operational leeway to deal with the circumstances that are in front of them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I think if you have someone who deliberately, maliciously and recklessly drove at a high speed a modified PMD, you would have to consider that quite differently from perhaps somebody who is on a family outing but who has then strayed away from their parent.

sections.label: Support and public education
sections.summary: The passage states progress will be made to support those relying on this for livelihood and to educate Singaporeans about the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I think we will progress as best we can so that those who do rely on this for their livelihood can be supported in some way.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And we will make sure that all Singaporeans are well educated about the provisions of this Bill and the enforcement of its provisions.
